title: Bacon and Egg Sandwich
subtitle: Back bacon and fried egg in a soft roll with ketchup or brown sauce
excerpt: The bacon and egg sandwich is back bacon and a fried egg in a soft white roll, finished with ketchup or brown sauce. The egg yolk should still be slightly runny so it breaks and runs into the bread when you bite. It is the standard British weekend breakfast sandwich.
sourceNotes: Fried bacon and egg sandwiches are a British breakfast staple documented throughout the twentieth century. The soft white roll filled with back bacon and egg is the standard format for British workmen's breakfast sandwiches and greasy-spoon cafes.

content.text: A bacon and egg sandwich is back bacon rashers and a fried egg in a soft white roll, with ketchup or brown sauce on top. The egg is what distinguishes it from a plain bacon roll: the runny yolk that breaks when you bite is the whole point. Back bacon is the standard British choice, giving a mix of lean meat and fat rather than the pure fat of streaky rashers.

Heat the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the {{back-bacon}} bacon rashers and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until the bacon is cooked through and the fat has rendered and coloured. Push to the edge of the pan.

Add {{sunflower-oil}} of oil to the cleared centre and crack in {{eggs}} eggs. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are fully set but the yolk is still runny. Tilt the pan and baste the top of the yolk with the hot oil from the edge a few times to set the surface.
Split the rolls and lay two bacon rashers in each. Set a fried egg on top of the bacon. Add ketchup or brown sauce and eat immediately.

items.symptom: The egg yolk sets solid before the white is cooked
items.cause: The pan was too hot, cooking the yolk from the bottom before the white had set.
items.fix: Cook the egg over a medium rather than high heat, and baste the top of the yolk with hot oil from the edge of the pan to set it gently from above.

items.symptom: The bacon is chewy and pale
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough before the bacon went in.
items.fix: The pan should be properly hot before adding the bacon. It should start to sizzle immediately. A few minutes of patience produces crisp fat and browned meat.

items.symptom: The egg slides out when eating
items.cause: The roll is too deep, or the bacon is not flat under the egg.
items.fix: Flatten the bacon rashers as they cook by pressing them lightly with a spatula. A shallow soft roll is better than a thick-sided one for containing a fried egg.

content.text: The bacon and egg sandwich is the standard British workmen's breakfast sandwich, served in greasy-spoon cafes, motorway service stations, and home kitchens across the country. The debate between ketchup and brown sauce is a long-running British cultural question with no correct answer. Soft white rolls or sliced white bread are the standard; sourdough or ciabatta, though common in cafes, are not the traditional format. The sandwich is best eaten immediately while the yolk is still warm and runny.
